name: Clark Stith
occupation: Attorney; has practiced law in Rock Springs since 1997 (SweetwaterNOW, March 21, 2014)
education: Bachelor's degrees in electrical engineering and philosophy, University of Kansas, 1985; Fulbright study at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, 1985–86; J.D., Georgetown University Law Center, 1991; M.S. in Foreign Service, Georgetown University, 1992 (SweetwaterNOW, March 21, 2014)
prior_offices: Wyoming House of Representatives, District 48, 2017–2024; House Speaker Pro Tempore, 2023–2024 (Wyoming Legislature member profile). He was not elected to the Secretary of State office he sought in 2014.
background: Clark Stith is a Rock Springs attorney who represented House District 48 in the Wyoming House of Representatives from 2017 to 2024 and served as House Speaker Pro Tempore in 2023–2024 (Wyoming Legislature member profile). The same official profile lists his birthplace as Atchison, Kansas. He lost the 2024 Republican primary for the House District 48 seat.

A March 21, 2014 SweetwaterNOW article on his Republican candidacy for secretary of state said he had practiced law in Rock Springs since 1997; received a J.D. from Georgetown University Law Center in 1991, an M.S. in Foreign Service from Georgetown in 1992, and bachelor's degrees in electrical engineering and philosophy from the University of Kansas in 1985; and studied as a Fulbright scholar at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1985–86.
